title: What is known about 1RB0RA_1RC1RF_1LD0LC_1RA1LE_1RA0LC_---0RD
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RA_1RC1RF_1LD0LC_1RA1LE_1RA0LC_---0RD.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The tape has three parts. On the left is a short control word, 50 to 115 cells long in the first 5·108 steps. Next comes a block of about 150 copies of 1101 that has not changed since early in the run. On the right, copies of 1101 are added at a steady rate of one per sweep. The crossings of the right part are proved in Lean. The control word changes irregularly at each turn, and its dynamics are not understood, so the halting transition (F reading a 0) is not ruled out.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: Where a halt can come from
claims.text: If the machine halts on its third step from a configuration, that configuration is one of: A with 0 under the head, 1 right, 0 two right. So a run can reach a halt only through one of these patterns, and a proof that the machine never halts only has to rule them out. The proof splits on the state and the five cells around the head.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 53,279 cells have been visited and 32,920 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/linear
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.073). Right of the start it grows in proportion to the step count (the head drifts steadily that way) (fitted exponent 0.863).

claims.title: Crossing the right part
claims.text: A> (0111)^n → (1110)^n A>, F> (1101)^n → (1011)^n F>, B> (1110)^n → (1101)^n B>, for every n.

claims.title: Three parts
claims.text: In every 300th sample of D at the right end, from step 7.6·106 to 5.5·108, the tape is a control word of 47 to 115 cells, then (1101)^150 (149 or 150, in some phase), then a run of the same word whose length grows by exactly 300 copies from one printed sample to the next.

claims.title: Crossing the right part
claims.text: A> (0111)^n → (1110)^n A>, F> (1101)^n → (1011)^n F>, B> (1110)^n → (1101)^n B>, for every n.

claims.title: Three parts
claims.text: In every 300th sample of D at the right end, from step 7.6·106 to 5.5·108, the tape is a control word of 47 to 115 cells, then (1101)^150 (149 or 150, in some phase), then a run of the same word whose length grows by exactly 300 copies from one printed sample to the next.

claims.title: The control word never repeats
claims.text: At the 19,908 visits of D to the right end in the first 2·10<sup>9</sup> steps, the control word (the tape left of the first run of at least 100 copies of the four-cell word) takes 19,905 different values, none longer than 111 cells. So the left end is not a cycler. It looks like a slowly growing counter-like or chaotic word.
claims.where: tmrun M 2000000000 at D R, counted in Python

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The machine halts only when F reads a 0. F is entered from B on a 1, which happens at the turns on the control word. The control word evolves irregularly and has no known invariant. CTL (windows of 2 to 5 cells) and NGramCPS (widths 2 to 8, history, LRU) fail.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

sections.heading: Control word, frozen block, growing wall
html: Each sweep the head crosses the right part (A, F and B cross whole runs of the word, proved in Lean), adds one copy at the right end, and runs back to the left. Since a sweep costs time proportional to the tape, the right part grows like the square root of the step count.

sections.heading: An irregular control word
html:
It is rewritten at every turn and its length wanders between about 50 and 115 cells, growing very slowly. This is the side that grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2. The block of 150 copies of 1101 between the two parts was laid down early and has not changed since.

What halting would need. F reading a 0. F is entered from B reading a 1, which happens only at the control word. Deciding the machine means understanding the control word: as a counter, a finite system, or something chaotic.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.073). Right of the start it grows in proportion to the step count (the head drifts steadily that way) (fitted exponent 0.863).
After 109 steps the tape spans 53,279 cells (87 left of the start, 35,534 right), with a density of 1s of 0.618.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

summary: A bouncer whose right part is the word 1101 repeated, one more copy every sweep; it turns around at the left end on a short control word of blocks 110 and 100110 that keeps changing irregularly and grows very slowly; a block of 150 copies of 1101 stays frozen in between.
family: bouncer with a chaotic control word
